question.problem:
$$
f(x,z)=⟨x,\,\text{_____},\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(x,z)$ above parametrizes the hyperbolic paraboloid defined in Cartesian coordinates as $2y=8{z}^{2}-{x}^{2}.$ What is the second component of $f?$
question.worked_solution:
Solving our equation for $y,$ we obtain

$$
2y=8{z}^{2}-{x}^{2}\,⟹\,y=4{z}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨x,\,4{z}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2},\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $x\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $4{z}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}.$
